notes.en: He lived at a little distance from his body, regarding his own acts with doubtful side-glances.
notes.source: James Joyce · A Painful Case, Dubliners · 1914

reference.context: 故事开篇描写达菲井然有序却孤立的生活。他习惯把自己当成第三人称来观察，与自己的身体和感受保持距离。这里写的是一个人物的疏离，邀请读者看见过度自我审视的代价。

notes.zh: 作家的秘密不在于灵感——因为灵感究竟来自何处，从来都不清楚——而在于他的执着与耐心。
notes.en: The writer’s secret is not inspiration – for it is never clear where it comes from – it is his stubbornness, his patience.
notes.source: Orhan Pamuk · My Father’s Suitcase (tr. Maureen Freely) · 2006-12-07

reference.context: 帕慕克由父亲留下的手稿谈起，写到自己多年独坐桌前、用词语一点点建造世界的经验。他随后以用针挖井的土耳其俗语说明这种耐心，把创造放回长期的手艺与劳动之中。
reference.question: 我是否一直在等待灵感，而没有给一件重要的事留下持续练习的时间？

notes.en: Love disguised itself as a question.

notes.en: And in a universe where we both agree that no one could love you, if we look hard enough, something will prove us wrong.

notes.en: It’s just that you make my life so much bigger, and I’m wondering if I do the same thing for you.

notes.en: The ultimate luxury now might be just a blank space in the calendar.

notes.zh: 主题可能改变，甚至让你捉摸不定；但既然你的人生是你自己的故事，你总能选择讲述它的语调。
notes.en: The theme you choose may change or simply elude you, but being your own story means you can always choose the tone.
notes.source: Toni Morrison · Wellesley College Commencement Address · 2004-05-28

reference.locator: Closing passage after acknowledging that no author completely controls a narrative

reference.originalText: The theme you choose may change or simply elude you, but being your own story means you can always choose the tone.
reference.context: 莫里森在演讲结尾把人生比作故事。她先承认作者也无法完全控制叙事与闯入其中的人物，再提出我们仍能选择讲述的语调，以怎样的语言理解自己和他人。

notes.zh:
来和我一起庆祝吧：
每一天，都有某种东西
试图将我杀死，
却没能成功。
notes.en:
come celebrate
with me that everyday
something has tried to kill me
and has failed.
notes.source: Lucille Clifton · won’t you celebrate with me (Collected Poems text) · 1991 text copyright
